name: Native (Swift and Kotlin)
summary: Two separate native apps: Swift and Xcode build the iPhone version, Kotlin and Android Studio build the Android version.

free_plan_covers.note: Xcode and Android Studio are both free downloads with no required paid service to build, run or ship an app.

first_paid_usd_month.note: No paid plan. Both IDEs are free. Store fees apply separately and are not counted here.

portability.note: Swift and Kotlin code share nothing with each other or with a cross-platform tool, so switching later means rewriting both apps.

language.note: Two separate codebases: Swift for iOS, and Kotlin, Google's recommended language, for Android.

shares_react_skills.note: Neither platform uses React. Screens are built with SwiftUI or UIKit on iOS, and Jetpack Compose or Views on Android.

needs_mac_for_ios.note: Xcode, the only tool that builds and signs iOS apps, requires macOS on a Mac with an Apple M1 chip or newer.

setup.step: Install Xcode from the Mac App Store and create a new iOS App project in Swift.
Run it on the iOS Simulator or a connected iPhone to preview.
Install Android Studio and create a new Android project in Kotlin.
Run it on the Android Emulator or a connected phone to preview.
Archive and sign each app separately: Xcode's Organizer for the App Store, Android Studio's release build for Google Play.

builder_notes: Never hardcode API keys in Info.plist, xcconfig files, BuildConfig or strings.xml. An IPA or APK can be unzipped, so anything embedded at build time is readable.
Call anything that needs a private key from your own backend. Use Keychain on iOS and the Keystore system on Android only for secrets issued to a signed-in user, not build-time API keys.
